summary: A scaling benchmark did not distinguish a correct repeated-slicing quadratic implementation, while locating the last delimiter in the worst case has a matching linear lower bound that directly certifies the candidate's optimality.

optimality.argument: For a length-n string containing one word and no spaces, any unchecked character could instead be a space and change the last word's length, so a correct algorithm must inspect Omega(n) characters in the worst case. The candidate moves one cursor left across the trailing spaces and final word without revisiting a position, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: On an all-letter string, every position before the end must be ruled out as the final delimiter; an unread position could change the required length.
The two backward phases share one monotone cursor, and each character is visited at most once before the answer is returned.
The three source-fidelity-verified examples exercise no trailing spaces, multiple trailing spaces, and a longer final word; black-box real-test execution passed all eight existing correctness checks.
